angle: follow the sign-in: an employee signs in once and gets a role in each account (IAM Identity Center), the identity source decides where the password is checked, direct federation is the per-account alternative and the emergency path, Active Directory reaches AWS as a real directory, a proxy or a small Samba directory (Directory Service), and an app user signs in to a user pool that issues tokens, while an identity pool turns a token into AWS credentials (Cognito)

Pattern: _build/style/exemplar/iam-1-fast.md and iam-2-deep.md (subsection order U1, Say it U2, Check and Recap U4), _build/work/10-vpc/brief.json (brief shape). Chapter 03 already teaches IAM Identity Center and Cognito in two short subsections (03-iam/2-deep.md) and owns the trap ids iam-trap-cognito-vs-identity-center, iam-trap-onprem-ad-needs-aws-directory, iam-trap-iam-users-for-people, iam-trap-role-long-term-credentials and iam-trap-keys-on-instance; this chapter goes deeper, never repeats those trap texts, and may cite those ids in distractors.

sections.heading: Predict
sections.plan: One plain line ('Guess before you read. The answers are in the Check section.'), then two prompts, each ending with '?'. Predict 1 is the gist trap (<!-- gist-trap -->): 'Your employees already sign in to a business app through your corporate identity provider. Can an Amazon Cognito user pool connected to that provider give them sign-in to the AWS Management Console of your accounts?' (common sense says yes, because Cognito is sign-in; the answer is no). Predict 2: 'A company connects its on-premises Active Directory to AWS with AD Connector. Where are the users' passwords checked when they sign in to an AWS application?' No term is defined in a prompt; no answers here (U4).

sections.heading: Look first
sections.plan: One or two sentences: open AWS CloudShell and look for the roles that IAM Identity Center creates, and for IAM users. Then the task region <!-- task:start id=identity-federation-t01 --> <!-- task:end -->. At most 30 words of prose.

sections.heading: In one breath
sections.plan: 1) Say it callout, at most 25 words, two sentences: IAM Identity Center gives your employees single sign-on to AWS accounts; Amazon Cognito signs in the users of the apps you build. Link the workforce fact (display 'single sign-on experience of your employees' reads badly mid-sentence; use 'including any AWS accounts that are assigned' or keep the link on the Cognito half: [an identity platform for web and mobile apps] (cognito-identity-platform-definition)). 2) **The problem it solves.** One sentence: without them, each account needs its own IAM users and each app stores its own passwords. 3) **Predict the picture.** 'Which path does an employee take, and which path does an app user take?' then the hero identity-federation-hero inside a 'Show the picture' reveal, with alt, **Figure.** caption and the 4 numbered steps exactly as in diagrams below. 4) Startup example callout with the Problem of data/startup.json chapter 05 word for word (36 words plus the label).

sections.heading: Words that go together
sections.plan: One words table with 4 rows (Term | Words that go with it | Plain meaning | Do not confuse with). Rows: identity provider (IdP): you **federate** with an identity provider | the system that checks who a person is | identity source (where IAM Identity Center reads users). permission set: **assign** a permission set to a group for an account | a template of policies that becomes a role in each account | IAM role (what IAM Identity Center creates from it). user pool: users **sign in** to a user pool | the user directory of your app; it issues tokens | identity pool. identity pool: an identity pool **exchanges** a token for AWS credentials | gives app users temporary AWS credentials | user pool. None of the four terms is in data/terms.json yet: write <!-- needs-term: <term> --> at first use until the orchestrator adds them (term_requests). Cell 2 bolds only the partner word.

Answer: No; Cognito is for [customer identity and access management (CIAM)] in the apps you build (cognito-decision-guide-ciam-for-apps-you-build); IAM Identity Center is for the workforce. **Predict 1:** No: Cognito is [not a supported identity source] of IAM Identity Center (iam-identity-center-cognito-is-not-an-identity-source); use IAM Identity Center for employees. sections.heading: How it works
sections.minutes: sum of the six subsection time boxes (26)
sections.order_note: Teaching order follows one sign-in. An employee signs in once and gets a role in each account (1); the identity source decides where that password is checked (2); direct federation is the per-account way and the emergency path (3); Active Directory reaches AWS through one of three directory options (4); an app user signs in to a user pool, and an identity pool turns the token into AWS credentials (5); a user pool federates outside providers and its tokens protect the API (6). Mark subsections 1, 4 and 5 with <!-- section: route=pass -->: the core questions review them.

sections.heading: IAM Identity Center turns one sign-in into a role session in each account

plan.problem: An engineer with an IAM user in each of seven accounts has seven passwords and seven sets of keys, and removing that engineer means seven deletions.
trace: **Enable.** An administrator enables an organization instance in the AWS Organizations management account: it is the only instance type that can [manage access to AWS accounts] (iam-identity-center-org-instance-only-one-for-account-access), and the organization needs [all AWS Organizations features are enabled] (iam-identity-center-needs-organizations-all-features). Name the former name once here: formerly [AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO)] (iam-identity-center-change-renamed-from-aws-sso-2022-07).

**Assign.** The administrator assigns a user or group a permission set for an account; a permission set is [a template that you create and maintain] (iam-identity-center-permission-set-is-policy-template) that holds AWS managed, customer managed or inline policies (iam-identity-center-permission-set-policy-types).

**Create the role.** IAM Identity Center [creates and manages IAM roles] in each assigned account, one per permission set (iam-identity-center-creates-roles-per-permission-set-not-iam-users); their names begin with AWSReservedSSO_ (iam-identity-center-roles-named-awsreservedsso).

**Sign in and work.** The user signs in once to the AWS access portal, which [creates an authentication session], and opens every assigned account [without additional sign ins] (iam-identity-center-one-sign-in-all-assignments); the session in an account uses temporary credentials [generated every time you sign in] (iam-identity-center-users-get-temporary-credentials), also in the AWS CLI v2, where [the CLI manages short-term credentials automatically] (iam-identity-center-cli-v2-sign-in-short-term-credentials).
plan.table: What the administrator defines and what appears in each account (columns: You define | In each assigned account | The user gets): a user or group | no IAM user, no IAM group | one sign-in; a permission set | one IAM role, AWSReservedSSO_ | the role's permissions; an assignment of a permission set to a user for an account | the role trusts IAM Identity Center | a role session with temporary credentials. The middle cell of row 1 links [does not create IAM users and groups] (iam-identity-center-creates-roles-per-permission-set-not-iam-users).
plan.why: Why roles underneath? IAM users [are granted long-term credentials] while IAM Identity Center users get temporary ones (iam-identity-center-users-get-temporary-credentials), so a change happens in one place: when a permission set changes, the [corresponding IAM policies and roles are updated accordingly] (iam-identity-center-permission-set-change-updates-roles).
plan.exam_signal: "employees sign in once to many AWS accounts" with "corporate identities" points to IAM Identity Center with permission sets, which [configures all the necessary user permissions] in the accounts (iam-identity-center-configures-account-permissions-automatically).
plan.body_extras: Optional half sentence if the budget allows: a customer managed policy in a permission set must exist in each account first, or IAM Identity Center [fails to assign the permission set] (iam-identity-center-customer-managed-policy-must-preexist).

go_deeper.title: sessions outlive sign-out
go_deeper.content: At most 80 words. A role session [operate independently once established] and lasts [up to 12 hours] (iam-identity-center-role-sessions-persist-up-to-12-hours). After sign-out, application sessions end [within approximately 30 minutes] (iam-identity-center-signout-app-sessions-end-within-30-minutes). A disabled user with a portal session [can continue to assume new roles] until the assignments are removed (iam-identity-center-disabled-user-keeps-assuming-roles). To cut access at once, add the user to a Deny statement in an SCP and keep it 12 hours (iam-identity-center-revoke-keep-deny-12-hours, display [If you wait 12 hours]); an administrator can also end the user's session (iam-identity-center-admin-can-end-user-session).

plan.say_it: The short answer is: one sign-in, then a role in each account. The thing to watch is the permission set, because it becomes that role.
plan.stop_and_answer: A permission set lets engineers read Amazon S3 in five accounts. An administrator adds DynamoDB read access to the permission set. Must someone create new IAM users or roles in the five accounts? Answer: No. IAM Identity Center updates the roles it created: the [corresponding IAM policies and roles are updated accordingly] (iam-identity-center-permission-set-change-updates-roles).

sections.heading: The identity source decides where users live and who checks passwords

plan.problem: The employees already exist in a corporate directory. IAM Identity Center must know them without a second password for each person.
trace: **Default.** At first enablement IAM Identity Center uses the [Identity Center directory as your default identity source] (iam-identity-center-default-identity-source-directory): users and passwords live in IAM Identity Center, with MFA [turned on by default] (iam-identity-center-mfa-on-by-default).

**Active Directory.** Connect it with [use AD Connector] or an [AWS Managed Microsoft AD trust relationship] (iam-identity-center-on-prem-ad-two-options); IAM Identity Center uses [pass-through authentication to the source AD instance], and [No password information is synchronized] (iam-identity-center-ad-pass-through-no-passwords-synced).

**External identity provider.** With Okta or Microsoft Entra ID, SAML 2.0 signs the user in, and SCIM gives [automatic provisioning (synchronization) of user and group information] (iam-identity-center-scim-automatic-provisioning); IAM Identity Center holds [no authentication material] (iam-identity-center-external-idp-no-passwords-stored), and identities [must be provisioned into IAM Identity Center] before you assign them (iam-identity-center-provision-before-assign).

**One source.** IAM Identity Center connects [only one directory or one SAML 2.0 identity provider] at a time (iam-identity-center-one-identity-source-at-a-time); changing it [might remove all user and group assignments] (iam-identity-center-change-source-may-remove-assignments).
plan.table: Truth table (columns: Identity source | Where users live | Who checks the password): Identity Center directory | IAM Identity Center | IAM Identity Center; Active Directory | your AD | your AD, by pass-through (iam-identity-center-ad-pass-through-no-passwords-synced); external IdP | the IdP, copied in by SCIM | the IdP (iam-identity-center-external-idp-no-passwords-stored).
plan.why: Why keep the password at the source? One place checks it, so a reset or a leaver is handled once, in the directory the company already runs; IAM Identity Center keeps [no authentication material] (iam-identity-center-external-idp-no-passwords-stored).
plan.exam_signal: "users already exist in an external identity provider and must be provisioned automatically" points to SAML 2.0 for sign-in plus SCIM, which syncs from [System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM)] providers such as Okta and Microsoft Entra ID (iam-identity-center-scim-automatic-sync).
plan.body_extras: Optional, one clause, written as 'IAM Identity Center [does not support SAMBA4-based Simple AD]' (iam-identity-center-simple-ad-not-identity-source).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: users stay in the directory you already have. The thing to watch is that you connect one source at a time.
plan.stop_and_answer: A company connects Okta to IAM Identity Center with SAML, but SCIM is off. A new engineer exists only in Okta. Can an administrator assign her a permission set today? Answer: Not yet. Identities [must be provisioned into IAM Identity Center] first (iam-identity-center-provision-before-assign), by SCIM or by hand. Do not link the NameID display of iam-identity-center-saml-nameid-must-match-username: it holds bold markup.

sections.heading: Direct SAML federation works per account while Identity Center federates once

plan.problem: Before IAM Identity Center, companies sent employees from their identity provider straight to IAM roles. The exam still asks when that is the right answer.
trace: **Trust the provider.** In one account you [create an identity provider entity] for an IdP that speaks [OpenID Connect (OIDC) or SAML 2.0] (iam-federation-idp-entity-oidc-or-saml).

**Map people to roles.** Users [assume IAM roles] in that account (iam-identity-center-decision-guide-federation-with-iam), so the console needs no IAM user: [without an IAM user for everyone in the organization] (iam-federation-saml-console-sso-without-iam-users).

**Directory variant.** With AWS Directory Service, you assign IAM roles to directory users or groups, and [your directory must have an access URL] (directory-service-console-access-iam-roles-access-url); AD Connector does it [without setting up SAML infrastructure] (directory-service-ad-connector-console-without-saml). This is what the exam guide calls federating a directory service with IAM roles.

**Many accounts.** Repeat both steps in every account, or federate once with IAM Identity Center: [you only federate once] and have [only one certificate to manage] (iam-identity-center-one-point-of-federation).
plan.table: Columns: Approach | You set it up | Fits when. IAM federation with SAML or OIDC | in each account | a few accounts, or an emergency path; Directory Service with IAM roles | for each directory | directory users need the console of one account; IAM Identity Center | once for the organization | many accounts in AWS Organizations. Link the two levels in one cell: [direct federation to each AWS account] versus [single sign-on to multiple AWS accounts] (iam-identity-center-wa-two-federation-approaches).
plan.why: Why keep direct federation when IAM Identity Center exists? It does not depend on IAM Identity Center: AWS's emergency access option signs users in [through direct federation] (iam-identity-center-emergency-access-direct-federation), and the two can run side by side (iam-identity-center-coexists-with-iam-federation).
plan.exam_signal: "Active Directory users must sign in to the AWS Management Console with their AD credentials" and "no IAM users" points to IAM roles for directory users (directory-service-console-sso-iam-roles); across many accounts of an organization it points to IAM Identity Center instead (iam-identity-center-wa-two-federation-approaches).

go_deeper.title: when IAM Identity Center is unavailable
go_deeper.content: At most 80 words. Its data is [stored in the Region where you enabled it] (iam-identity-center-data-stored-in-enabled-region). Since [February 2, 2026] an organization instance can replicate to more Regions to [maintain account access with already provisioned permissions] (iam-identity-center-change-multi-region-2026-02, iam-identity-center-replication-keeps-access-in-regional-disruption), but [Multi-Region support is not available for Active Directory] (iam-identity-center-multi-region-not-with-active-directory). AWS still recommends break-glass access for [a small group of privileged users] (iam-identity-center-break-glass-recommended), and you must [deploy this configuration before a disruption occurs] (iam-identity-center-emergency-access-direct-federation). Do not let this replication decide a question: it is a change of the last 24 months.

plan.say_it: The short answer is: direct federation works one account at a time. The thing to watch is the number of accounts you must repeat it in.
plan.stop_and_answer: A company has one AWS account, does not use AWS Organizations, and runs AWS Managed Microsoft AD. Its administrators must use the console with their AD credentials and no IAM users. What do you set up? Answer: assign IAM roles to the AD users or groups and give the directory an access URL ([your directory must have an access URL], directory-service-console-access-iam-roles-access-url). IAM Identity Center would need an organization instance to reach accounts (iam-identity-center-org-instance-only-one-for-account-access).

sections.heading: The three Directory Service options differ in where the directory runs

plan.problem: Windows servers, file shares and SQL Server databases expect Active Directory. In AWS you choose how much of that directory AWS runs for you.
trace: **AWS Managed Microsoft AD.** It is [an actual Microsoft Windows Server Active Directory] (directory-service-managed-ad-actual-windows-server-ad): AWS creates [two domain controllers] in different Availability Zones of your VPC (directory-service-managed-ad-minimum-two-domain-controllers) and keeps [exclusive control of the Domain Administrator] (directory-service-managed-ad-no-domain-admin-for-customer).

**Trust.** It joins an on-premises forest with [one and two-way external and forest trust relationships] (directory-service-trust-types-and-directions) once the networks are connected (directory-service-trust-needs-network-connection-to-vpc); IAM Identity Center, WorkSpaces and the console need a [two-way trust is required] setup, while EC2, RDS and FSx work with [either a one-way or two-way trust] (directory-service-two-way-trust-for-aws-apps-one-way-for-ec2-rds-fsx).

**AD Connector.** [AD Connector is a proxy service] that [forwards sign-in requests to your on-premises Active Directory] (directory-service-ad-connector-is-a-proxy) [without caching any information in the cloud] (directory-service-ad-connector-gateway-no-caching); it needs a [(VPN) connection or Direct Connect] (directory-service-ad-connector-needs-vpn-or-direct-connect) and serves AWS applications [for AWS created applications and services only] (directory-service-ad-connector-aws-apps-only-no-third-party).

**Simple AD.** A standalone directory [powered by Samba 4] with basic features (directory-service-simple-ad-samba-4-basic-features); it is [no longer open to new customers] (directory-service-simple-ad-closed-to-new-customers).
plan.table: Truth table of workloads (columns: Workload | AWS Managed Microsoft AD | AD Connector): Amazon EC2 domain join | yes, at launch (directory-service-managed-ad-seamless-join-at-launch) | yes, then the instance [bypasses AD Connector] (directory-service-ad-connector-ec2-join-bypasses-connector); Amazon RDS for SQL Server | yes | no: RDS is [compatible with AWS Managed Microsoft AD only] (directory-service-rds-needs-managed-ad); FSx for Windows File Server | yes | no: [Amazon FSx does not support] AD Connector (directory-service-fsx-windows-needs-managed-ad-or-self-managed); IAM Identity Center sign-in | yes, also for many forests (iam-identity-center-one-ad-directory-managed-ad-for-multiple-forests) | yes, for [the single domain to which AD Connector attaches] (iam-identity-center-ad-connector-single-domain-no-portal-reset). Do not restate the fast compare table: this table is about workloads.
plan.why: Why a proxy at all? AD Connector [eliminates the need of directory synchronization] (directory-service-ad-connector-no-directory-sync): users, groups and passwords stay where the company manages them today.
plan.exam_signal: "Active Directory-aware workloads in AWS" or "Amazon RDS for SQL Server with Windows Authentication" points to AWS Managed Microsoft AD (directory-service-decision-guide-ad-dependent-workloads-row); "users must stay in the on-premises directory" with sign-in to AWS applications only points to AD Connector (directory-service-which-to-choose-row).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: Managed AD is a real directory, and AD Connector only forwards sign-ins. The thing to watch is which servers must join the domain.
plan.stop_and_answer: A company uses AD Connector for WorkSpaces. It now moves a SQL Server database to Amazon RDS with Windows Authentication. Can AD Connector alone serve the database? Answer: No. RDS is [compatible with AWS Managed Microsoft AD only] (directory-service-rds-needs-managed-ad); add AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a trust to the on-premises domain (directory-service-trust-types-and-directions).

sections.heading: A user pool signs users in and an identity pool hands out AWS credentials

plan.problem: A mobile app must know who the user is. Sometimes it must also upload straight to Amazon S3. These are two different jobs.
trace: **Sign in.** The user signs in to a user pool, a user directory that uses OIDC to [issue JSON web tokens (JWTs)] (cognito-user-pool-vs-identity-pool): [access tokens, ID tokens, and refresh tokens] (cognito-federated-user-profile-maps-idp-claims).

**Exchange.** The app sends a token to an identity pool, which exchanges it for [temporary, limited-privilege AWS credentials] (cognito-user-pool-vs-identity-pool) that come [temporary session credentials from AWS Security Token Service] (cognito-identity-pool-credentials-from-sts).

**Pick the role.** The identity pool uses an authenticated role or, for guests, an unauthenticated role; it can [issue limited-privilege credentials to guest users] (cognito-identity-pool-guest-credentials), whose permissions [should be more restrictive] (cognito-unauthenticated-role-more-restrictive).
**Call AWS.** The app calls Amazon S3 with those credentials; the user's identity ID in a bucket policy can limit each user to [access to their own folder] (cognito-identity-id-per-user-s3-folder).
plan.table: Columns: The app needs | User pool | Identity pool. Sign-up, sign-in and tokens for your API | yes | no; AWS credentials for signed-in users | yes, to sign in | yes, to exchange the token; AWS credentials for guests | no | yes, unauthenticated role; Sign-in with Google, and no direct AWS calls | yes | no. Under the table one sentence: [Neither component requires the other] (cognito-pools-used-together-or-alone).
plan.why: Why not put an access key in the app? The IAM guide says not to embed access keys in the app, [even in encrypted storage] (cognito-mobile-app-never-embed-access-keys); a key in an app ships to every phone, while identity pool credentials are temporary and limited to one role.
plan.exam_signal: "mobile app users upload directly to Amazon S3" or "temporary AWS credentials for app users" points to an identity pool, which AWS recommends [Whenever possible, use Amazon Cognito] over calling AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity yourself (cognito-preferred-over-direct-web-identity-federation); "sign-up and sign-in" alone points to a user pool.

go_deeper.title: how an identity pool picks the role
go_deeper.content: At most 80 words. The pool can use [a default role], [rules that query your user's claims], or [your user's group membership in a user pool] (cognito-identity-pool-role-selection-options). Rules run in order and [the first matching rule is used] (cognito-identity-pool-rules-first-match-then-role-resolution); with several groups, the role of [the best (lowest) Precedence value] wins (cognito-group-precedence-preferred-role; ask for a display without backticks if needed). Since 2025-08 a role that trusts the identity pools service needs an aud condition, [but aud is required] (cognito-identity-pool-trust-policy-aud-condition-enforced): the task identity-federation-t02 shows this error.

plan.say_it: The short answer is: the user pool proves who the user is, and the identity pool gives AWS access. The thing to watch is the guest role.
plan.stop_and_answer: A game lets people play before they sign in and saves their scores to DynamoDB straight from the phone. What do the guests need? Answer: an identity pool with an unauthenticated role; it can [issue limited-privilege credentials to guest users] (cognito-identity-pool-guest-credentials). No user pool is needed until they sign in.

sections.heading: A user pool federates outside providers and issues its own tokens to the app

plan.problem: A business customer wants its staff to use their company sign-in in your app, so your app should never see their passwords.
trace: **Redirect.** The user picks the company's sign-in on managed login, [managed login, an update to the hosted UI] (cognito-change-managed-login-2024-11; this is the one use of the former name), and goes to the company's SAML 2.0 identity provider.
**Assert.** The provider signs the user in and returns a SAML assertion; to that provider, [Amazon Cognito is a service provider (SP)] (cognito-federated-user-profile-maps-idp-claims).
**Map.** Cognito maps the claims to a user profile: [Federated and local users have a user profile] (cognito-user-pool-federated-users-get-profile-and-jwt).

**Issue.** The user pool [issues JSON web tokens (JWTs)] of its own (cognito-saml-idp-must-support-saml-2), so the app can [standardize your app on one set of JWTs] (cognito-user-pool-federated-users-get-profile-and-jwt).

**Check at the door.** API Gateway checks the token with [an authorizer of the COGNITO_USER_POOLS type] (cognito-api-gateway-cognito-user-pools-authorizer); an Application Load Balancer can sign users in before forwarding, [supported only with HTTPS listeners] (cognito-alb-authenticate-cognito-https-only).
plan.table: Columns: Front door | What it checks | Result. API Gateway with a COGNITO_USER_POOLS authorizer | the user pool token in the Authorization header | the call succeeds only if [the supplied token is valid] (cognito-api-gateway-cognito-user-pools-authorizer); API Gateway with AWS_IAM | a request signed with identity pool credentials (cognito-api-gateway-aws-iam-with-identity-pool) | the IAM role's permissions decide; Application Load Balancer, HTTPS listener | an authenticate-cognito rule | the request reaches the targets after sign-in.
plan.why: Why does Cognito issue its own tokens? Each provider speaks its own format; one set of JWTs keeps the app code the same for Google, a SAML provider and local users (cognito-user-pool-federated-users-get-profile-and-jwt).
plan.exam_signal: "a partner's employees sign in to the company's web application with their corporate SAML identity provider" points to a user pool with a SAML provider, which gives single sign-on to [workforce identities in SAML 2.0 and OIDC IdPs] in your app (cognito-user-pool-workforce-sso-in-your-app); IAM Identity Center is for your own workforce's AWS access.
plan.spot_the_bug: **Spot the bug.** An Application Load Balancer listens on HTTP port 80. Its listener rule first authenticates users with a Cognito user pool, then forwards to the targets. What is wrong? Answer: the authenticate-cognito action is [supported only with HTTPS listeners] (cognito-alb-authenticate-cognito-https-only); add an HTTPS listener with a certificate and redirect port 80 to it.
plan.say_it: The short answer is: the customer's provider checks the password, and Cognito gives your app its own tokens. The thing to watch is an HTTPS listener on the load balancer.
plan.stop_and_answer: A user pool already federates one partner's SAML provider. A second partner signs in with an OIDC provider. Does the app need code for a second token format? Answer: No. The user pool issues the same JWTs for every provider: [Federated and local users have a user profile] and get tokens from the user pool (cognito-user-pool-federated-users-get-profile-and-jwt, cognito-user-pool-sp-and-idp-dual-role).

sections.heading: FAQ quick-fire
sections.plan: Exactly 5 FAQ items from faq below. Each: the can-or-cannot question, a one-clause answer with a fact link, then an AWS quote block holding one whole sentence of the evidence quote, from the service FAQ URL.

traps.belief: A Cognito user pool connected to the corporate identity provider can give employees sign-in to the AWS accounts.
traps.truth: Cognito manages identities for customer-facing applications and is not a supported identity source of IAM Identity Center; employees reach AWS accounts through IAM Identity Center.
traps.note: Deeper than chapter 03's iam-trap-cognito-vs-identity-center (which says only that they serve different users): this one is the wiring mistake of connecting Cognito to Identity Center or to the console.

traps.belief: After users sign in to a Cognito user pool, the app can call Amazon S3 or DynamoDB with the user pool tokens.
traps.truth: A user pool issues JSON web tokens for your app or API; an identity pool exchanges a token for temporary, limited-privilege AWS credentials.

traps.belief: AD Connector copies the on-premises users and passwords into AWS.
traps.truth: AD Connector is a proxy: it forwards sign-in requests to the on-premises domain controllers, caches nothing in the cloud and replicates no directory data.

traps.belief: IAM Identity Center creates an IAM user for each employee in each assigned account.
traps.truth: IAM Identity Center does not create IAM users or groups; it creates one IAM role per permission set in each assigned account.
traps.form: > **Exam trap:** <belief in plain words>. <truth with link [does not create IAM users and groups]>. <!-- trap: identity-federation-trap-idc-creates-iam-users -->

traps.belief: IAM Identity Center can use Active Directory for one team and Okta for another at the same time.
traps.truth: IAM Identity Center connects only one directory or one SAML 2.0 identity provider at a time, and changing the source might remove all assignments.
traps.form: Exam trap callout; the new case is the second team, not a restatement of the trace step: say what happens to assignments when an administrator switches the source.

traps.belief: Simple AD is a low-cost Active Directory that can trust the on-premises domain.
traps.truth: Simple AD does not support trust relationships, MFA or schema extensions; a trust with an on-premises domain needs AWS Managed Microsoft AD.

traps.belief: A one-way trust from AWS Managed Microsoft AD to the on-premises domain is enough for IAM Identity Center sign-in.
traps.truth: IAM Identity Center needs a two-way trust; one-way trusts do not work with it, although EC2, RDS and FSx work with either direction.
traps.form: Exam trap callout after the simple-ad one; link [One-way trusts do not work] (iam-identity-center-needs-two-way-trust-not-one-way).

traps.belief: An IAM identity provider and IAM roles in every account, with a custom credential broker, are as little work as a managed sign-in service.
traps.truth: Direct federation is repeated in each AWS account and needs your own broker code; IAM Identity Center federates once for an organization, and the IAM guide says to use Amazon Cognito whenever possible for app users.
traps.note: Question-only trap, added by questions-05-1 (Q205). Cited by q01, q04, q06.

traps.belief: An access key is safe inside a mobile app when the app stores the key encrypted.
traps.truth: The IAM guide says not to embed access keys with the app, even in encrypted storage; the app gets temporary credentials through Amazon Cognito.
traps.note: Question-only trap, added by questions-05-1 (Q205). Cited by q02.

traps.belief: On-premises Active Directory users can reach AWS applications only through a directory that runs in AWS.
traps.truth: When on-premises users only sign in to AWS applications, AD Connector forwards the sign-in requests to the on-premises domain controllers; AWS Managed Microsoft AD is for workloads that need a real domain in AWS.
traps.note: Question-only trap, added by questions-05-1 (Q205). Cited by q03.

traps.belief: AD Connector lets Amazon RDS for SQL Server use the accounts of the on-premises domain.
traps.truth: Amazon RDS is compatible with AWS Managed Microsoft AD only and is not compatible with AD Connector.
traps.note: Question-only trap, added by questions-05-1 (Q205). Cited by q08.

traps.belief: API Gateway needs custom authorizer code to check the tokens of a Cognito user pool.
traps.truth: A COGNITO_USER_POOLS authorizer lets API Gateway validate the user pool token without custom code; the call succeeds only if the token is valid.
traps.note: Question-only trap, added by questions-05-1 (Q205). Cited by q05.

traps.belief: An account instance of IAM Identity Center can give users access to the AWS account with permission sets.
traps.truth: Only an organization instance can manage access to AWS accounts; permission sets are available only for organization instances.
traps.note: Question-only trap, added by questions-05-1 (Q205). Cited by q07.

traps.belief: An Application Load Balancer can authenticate users with Cognito on any listener, HTTP included.
traps.truth: The authenticate-cognito and authenticate-oidc actions are supported only with HTTPS listeners.
traps.note: Question-only trap, added by questions-05-1 (Q205). Cited by q10.

faq.q: Does enabling IAM Identity Center change your existing IAM roles, users or policies?

story.trigger: Seven accounts would mean seven IAM users for each engineer. The bank also wants its 400 supervisors to sign in with the bank's identity provider.
story.problem: Callvale's 14 engineers need one sign-in for seven AWS accounts, with no long-term credentials. Separately, 400 bank employees must sign in to the Callvale web application with their corporate identities. Callvale must not store their passwords.
story.state_at_month_18: Seven accounts exist (chapter 04, same month). Engineers still sign in as the IAM users of stage 1 (chapter 03); those IAM users are deleted in this chapter. The Cognito user pool exists since stage 2 (chapter 33) for customers' dashboard users; this chapter adds a SAML provider (the bank's) to it. Chen is the security lead and may appear. AWS Directory Service arrives only at stage 4 for Peldon (chapters 23 and 39): it is never part of this chapter's story, its decision record or its diagrams.
story.rules: Question stems never name Callvale, Ana, Ben, Chen, the bank or Peldon. The story never teaches a fact. No dollar amounts. Ben's question is speak item identity-federation-s01, word for word. 'Callvale's identity provider' stays unnamed (no vendor names, STARTUP A8).

decision_record.context: The trigger of data/startup.json chapter 05 word for word (25 words). Then the before embed.
decision_record.requirement: Callvale's 14 engineers need one sign-in for seven AWS accounts, with no long-term credentials, and Callvale must not store the bank supervisors' passwords. Which solution has the LEAST operational overhead?
options: IAM users in one account who assume roles in the others
**IAM Identity Center connected to Callvale's identity provider, with Cognito federation for the bank** (chosen)
decision_record.decision: IAM Identity Center with permission sets for engineers: it [creates and manages IAM roles] in each account (iam-identity-center-creates-roles-per-permission-set-not-iam-users), and engineers get temporary credentials (iam-identity-center-users-get-temporary-credentials). Amazon Cognito federation for the bank's supervisors: the existing user pool adds the bank's SAML provider, and to that provider [Amazon Cognito is a service provider (SP)] (cognito-federated-user-profile-maps-idp-claims). The stage 1 IAM users are deleted. Then the after embed.
decision_record.tradeoff: All AWS access depends on the identity provider. Callvale must keep one tested emergency access path, set up [through direct federation] (iam-identity-center-emergency-access-direct-federation).
reasons_with_facts: Option 1 multiplies long-term credentials by seven; IAM users [are granted long-term credentials] (iam-identity-center-users-get-temporary-credentials).
Option 2 still keeps one IAM user with long-term credentials per engineer.
Option 3 meets both parts: one sign-in with temporary credentials for engineers, and no stored passwords for the supervisors, because the bank's provider authenticates them.
decision_record.word_note: Fields at most 115 words; the two embeds have no steps (see budgets).

question_slots.twin: first of strict twin pair 1 (twin q06)
question_slots.note: A company uses AWS Organizations with 12 accounts and an external SAML 2.0 identity provider for its employees; it also runs a mobile app for customers. Changed phrase: 'The engineers must sign in once and use the AWS CLI with short-term credentials in every account.' Key: IAM Identity Center with the SAML provider as identity source and permission sets. Options identical to q06, in neutral words that fit both stems: (1) IAM Identity Center with the identity provider as identity source, access by permission sets; (2) a Cognito user pool federated with the identity providers that the users already use, plus an identity pool for temporary AWS credentials (sibling-confusion, identity-federation-trap-cognito-for-workforce); (3) an IAM user with MFA and an access key for each person in each account (violates-qualifier and the no-long-term-credentials constraint, iam-trap-iam-users-for-people); (4) an IAM SAML identity provider and roles in every account, with a custom broker that calls AssumeRole (violates-qualifier, misconception: per-account federation is the least overhead).

A mobile app already signs users in with a Cognito user pool. Users must now upload photos directly to an S3 bucket, each to their own prefix; no AWS keys may be stored in the app. MOST secure. Key: add an identity pool with the user pool as provider and an authenticated role scoped to the user's prefix (cognito-user-pool-vs-identity-pool, cognito-identity-id-per-user-s3-folder). Distractors: sign the S3 requests with the user pool ID token (identity-federation-trap-user-pool-gives-aws-credentials, wrong-configuration); store an IAM user's access key encrypted in the app (iam-trap-iam-users-for-people, with cognito-mobile-app-never-embed-access-keys: [even in encrypted storage]); an identity pool whose authenticated role allows s3:PutObject on the whole bucket (violates-qualifier: it works, but every user can write every prefix).

question_slots.twin: first of strict twin pair 2 (twin q08)
question_slots.note: A company has an on-premises Active Directory and a Site-to-Site VPN to a VPC. Changed phrase: 'Employees must sign in to Amazon WorkSpaces with their existing AD credentials, and user accounts must remain only in the on-premises directory.' Key: AD Connector (directory-service-ad-connector-is-a-proxy, directory-service-ad-connector-no-data-replicated). Options identical to q08: (1) AD Connector in the VPC that points to the on-premises domain controllers; (2) AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a two-way forest trust to the on-premises domain (violates-qualifier here); (3) Simple AD with a trust to the on-premises domain (impossible-feature, identity-federation-trap-simple-ad-trusts, directory-service-simple-ad-unsupported-features); (4) a self-managed AD domain controller on EC2 that replicates the on-premises domain (violates-qualifier and the 'remain only on premises' constraint). State the side not tested: the VPN already reaches the domain controllers.

A company moves its workforce identities from on-premises Active Directory (connected to IAM Identity Center through AD Connector) to Okta. Employees must sign in with Okta, and new hires must appear in IAM Identity Center automatically, with the LEAST operational overhead. Which combination (Select TWO.)? Keys: change the identity source to the external identity provider with SAML 2.0 (iam-identity-center-one-identity-source-at-a-time); turn on automatic provisioning with SCIM (iam-identity-center-scim-automatic-provisioning). Distractors: keep AD Connector and add Okta as a second identity source (impossible-feature, identity-federation-trap-idc-two-sources-at-once); create an IAM SAML identity provider in every member account (violates-qualifier); connect Okta to a Cognito user pool and make it the identity source (sibling-confusion, identity-federation-trap-cognito-for-workforce). Explanation mentions that a change of source might remove assignments (iam-identity-center-change-source-may-remove-assignments).

A web app's users sign in to a Cognito user pool. Its REST API in API Gateway must accept requests only from signed-in users, with the LEAST development effort. Key: a COGNITO_USER_POOLS authorizer on the methods; the client sends the token in the Authorization header (cognito-api-gateway-cognito-user-pools-authorizer). Distractors: AWS_IAM authorization with an IAM user for each customer (iam-trap-iam-users-for-people, from chapter 03); a Lambda authorizer that validates the JWT in custom code (violates-qualifier); an AWS WAF rule that allows only known IP addresses (different-problem, misconception 'WAF knows who signed in').

question_slots.twin: twin_of q01 (strict: same stem and same four options as q01, one phrase changed)
question_slots.note: Changed phrase: 'The app's customers must sign in with their Google or Apple accounts and upload photos directly to Amazon S3 with short-term credentials.' Key moves to the Cognito option (user pool federated with the providers plus identity pool). The IAM Identity Center option now carries identity-federation-trap-cognito-for-workforce in the reverse direction (IAM Identity Center for customers). Place at least 3 questions between q01 and q06.

A company has one AWS account, does not use AWS Organizations and does not plan to; it runs AWS Managed Microsoft AD. Administrators must use the AWS Management Console with their AD credentials; the company wants to avoid IAM users. Key: assign IAM roles to AD groups and enable the directory's access URL (directory-service-console-access-iam-roles-access-url, directory-service-console-sso-iam-roles). Distractors: IAM users with the same names and passwords as in AD (iam-trap-iam-users-for-people); an account instance of IAM Identity Center with permission sets (impossible-feature: only an organization instance can manage access to AWS accounts, iam-identity-center-org-instance-only-one-for-account-access); a Cognito user pool with the directory as a SAML provider (identity-federation-trap-cognito-for-workforce).

question_slots.twin: twin_of q03 (strict: same stem and options, one phrase changed)
question_slots.note: Changed phrase: 'Amazon RDS for SQL Server databases must use Windows Authentication with the employees' existing AD accounts.' Key moves to AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a trust (directory-service-rds-needs-managed-ad, directory-service-two-way-trust-for-aws-apps-one-way-for-ec2-rds-fsx). AD Connector becomes impossible-feature (directory-service-ad-connector-not-rds-sql-server, identity-federation-trap-ad-connector-stores-users). Place at least 3 questions between q03 and q08.

A company has two on-premises AD forests and AWS Direct Connect to AWS. Employees from both forests must sign in to many accounts through IAM Identity Center; MOST operationally efficient. Key: AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the identity source, with two-way forest trusts to both forests (iam-identity-center-one-ad-directory-managed-ad-for-multiple-forests, iam-identity-center-needs-two-way-trust-not-one-way). Distractors: one AD Connector per forest, both connected to IAM Identity Center (impossible-feature: only one AD Connector directory at a time, identity-federation-trap-idc-two-sources-at-once); AWS Managed Microsoft AD with one-way trusts (identity-federation-trap-one-way-trust-for-idc, wrong-configuration); migrate both forests into AWS Managed Microsoft AD with ADMT first (violates-qualifier).

An internet-facing web application runs on EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer with an HTTPS listener. Business customers must sign in with their own corporate SAML identity providers before any request reaches the instances; LEAST development effort. Key: a Cognito user pool with the customers' SAML providers and an authenticate-cognito action in the HTTPS listener rule (cognito-alb-authenticate-cognito-https-only, cognito-saml-idp-must-support-saml-2). Distractors: add the customers' providers to IAM Identity Center as identity sources (identity-federation-trap-cognito-for-workforce reversed: Identity Center is for the workforce, and one source at a time); authenticate-cognito on a new HTTP listener on port 80 (wrong-configuration, misconception 'any listener can authenticate'); SAML handling written in the application code (violates-qualifier). The worked think-aloud (6 steps, about 200 words) shows the reader marking 'before any request reaches the instances' and 'LEAST development effort'.

Qualifier none. An administrator assigns a permission set to a group for an AWS account in IAM Identity Center. What does IAM Identity Center create in that account? Key: an IAM role for the permission set, whose name begins with AWSReservedSSO_ (iam-identity-center-creates-roles-per-permission-set-not-iam-users, iam-identity-center-roles-named-awsreservedsso). Options of 2 to 45 words (difficulty 1).

Qualifier none. A mobile game lets people play before they sign in and saves scores to DynamoDB directly from the device with temporary credentials. Which Cognito feature gives guests those credentials? Key: an identity pool with an unauthenticated role (cognito-identity-pool-guest-credentials, cognito-identity-pool-unauthenticated-guest-role). tasks.title: Find the roles that IAM Identity Center creates
tasks.kills: "IAM Identity Center creates an IAM user for each employee."
tasks.plan: In AWS CloudShell, read-only, 3 minutes, $0. Step 1: list IAM roles whose names begin with AWSReservedSSO_ (aws iam list-roles with a --query filter on RoleName); expected output stated first: one role per assigned permission set when the account gets access through IAM Identity Center, or an empty list otherwise (iam-identity-center-roles-named-awsreservedsso). Step 2: list IAM users (aws iam list-users, read-only) and see that none was created for the Identity Center users (iam-identity-center-creates-roles-per-permission-set-not-iam-users). Optional step 3: aws sso-admin list-instances (read-only), which may return nothing in an account without an instance. Creates nothing; commands must come from official CLI pages in the corpus (tasks check-cli --reference).

tasks.title: Create a user pool and an identity pool and see which one gives AWS credentials
tasks.kills: "A Cognito user pool hands AWS credentials to the app."
tasks.plan: In AWS CloudShell, 10 to 15 minutes, $0 (cognito-identity-pools-no-charge; user pools are billed by monthly active users and this task signs nobody in, cognito-user-pools-billed-by-mau). Create a user pool saa-identity-federation-t02 tagged book=saa and task=identity-federation-t02; create an app client without a secret; create an identity pool with the user pool as its provider, tagged with the two tags. Observe: the user pool holds users (zero now); describe the identity pool and read its providers: it [do not store any user profiles] (cognito-identity-pools-store-no-profiles). Break it: predict whether IAM accepts a role whose trust policy trusts cognito-identity.amazonaws.com with no aud condition; run create-role (tags book=saa, task=identity-federation-t02, name saa-identity-federation-t02-auth); expect an error; explain with [IAM returns an error] (cognito-identity-pool-trust-policy-aud-condition-enforced). Fix: create the role with the aud condition set to the identity pool ID and amr authenticated (cognito-identity-pool-role-trust-policy-aud-amr), then set it as the authenticated role of the identity pool. Do not call get-id or get-credentials-for-identity (no command prints credentials, T105). Cleanup in reverse order: delete the role, delete the identity pool, delete the app client, delete the user pool (if deletion protection is on, turn it off first; check the CLI default). Verify: the Resource Groups Tagging API filtered by task=identity-federation-t02 returns nothing; this needs fact request fr-0038 (Cognito resources in GetResources); GetResources does not return IAM roles (iam-tagging-api-getresources-no-iam-roles), so the role's deletion is shown by its cleanup step. Read-only alternative: list user pools and identity pools and describe one. Permissions: cognito-idp create and delete for user pools and clients, cognito-identity create, delete and set roles, iam:CreateRole, iam:DeleteRole, iam:PassRole on the role, iam:TagRole.

speak.prompt: What is the difference between IAM Identity Center and Cognito? Both look like sign-in to me.
speak.note: Compare starter 'Both ...' (J3): both sign people in, but for different doors. How it works: IAM Identity Center signs in our engineers and gives them a role in each AWS account; Cognito signs in the people who use our app and gives the app tokens. Watch: Cognito is not an identity source of IAM Identity Center, so the two stay separate. In your case: engineers through IAM Identity Center, the bank's supervisors through the user pool with the bank's provider. Question back: 'Does anyone outside Callvale need to reach an AWS account, or only the dashboard?' Must not say: 'Cognito can be the identity source of IAM Identity Center'; 'IAM Identity Center creates IAM users in each account'. Numbers in words only.

speak.prompt: Our users are in Active Directory in our office. Do we need AD Connector or AWS Managed Microsoft AD?
speak.note: Short answer: if your people only sign in to AWS applications, AD Connector; if servers in AWS must join a domain, AWS Managed Microsoft AD. How it works: AD Connector forwards each sign-in to your office domain controllers and keeps no copy; Managed AD is a real directory in your VPC that trusts your office directory. Watch: AD Connector needs a VPN or Direct Connect, and RDS for SQL Server and FSx for Windows File Server need Managed AD. Question back: 'Which servers or services in AWS must join your domain?' Must not say: 'AD Connector copies your users to AWS'; 'Simple AD can trust your office directory'.

cards.front: In AWS, employees must sign in once to many AWS accounts with their corporate identity provider. What do you use?
cards.back: IAM Identity Center with permission sets.

cards.front: In Amazon Cognito, user pool or identity pool: which one gives the app temporary AWS credentials?
In AWS Directory Service, AD Connector or AWS Managed Microsoft AD: which one keeps no directory data in AWS?
In IAM Identity Center, a new permission set has a session duration of {{c1::1 hour}} by default.
In IAM Identity Center, an AWS access portal session lasts {{c1::8 hours}} by default.
In AWS Directory Service, AWS creates {{c1::two domain controllers}} for each AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory.
In a Cognito identity pool (enhanced flow), the AWS credentials are {{c1::valid for one hour}}.
In a Cognito user pool, a refresh token expires {{c1::30 days}} after sign-in by default.
In IAM Identity Center, can a Cognito user pool be the identity source?
cards.back: No. Cognito is for customer-facing apps.

cards.front: In IAM Identity Center, can Okta and Active Directory be identity sources at the same time?
cards.back: No. One directory or one SAML provider at a time.

cards.front: In AWS Directory Service, can Simple AD have a trust with an on-premises domain?
cards.back: No. Use AWS Managed Microsoft AD.

cards.front: In IAM Identity Center with AWS Managed Microsoft AD, does a one-way trust to the on-premises domain work?
cards.back: No. IAM Identity Center needs a two-way trust.

diagrams.title: Two front doors: employees and app users
diagrams.claim: Employees reach AWS accounts through IAM Identity Center, while app users sign in to a Cognito user pool and reach AWS through an identity pool.
diagrams.alt: Two paths. Top: an employee signs in through an identity provider to IAM Identity Center, which opens a role in each assigned AWS account. Bottom: an app user signs in to a Cognito user pool, the app gets tokens, and an identity pool gives AWS credentials for Amazon S3.
say: An employee signs in once through the identity provider to IAM Identity Center.
IAM Identity Center opens a role in each assigned AWS account, created from a permission set.
An app user signs in to a Cognito user pool, which issues JSON web tokens (JWTs) to the app.
An identity pool exchanges the token for temporary AWS credentials, and the app calls Amazon S3.
diagrams.note: Step 2 links [creates and manages IAM roles] (iam-identity-center-creates-roles-per-permission-set-not-iam-users) in the Markdown; step 3 links [issue JSON web tokens (JWTs)]; step 4 links [temporary, limited-privilege AWS credentials] (cognito-user-pool-vs-identity-pool), or rewrite the step so the link text is that display. Nodes (9 of 12): employee, identity provider, IAM Identity Center, AWS account (role), app user, Cognito user pool, app, Cognito identity pool, Amazon S3. Two rows, flow left to right; numbered edges 1 to 4. The identity provider is a generic box, no vendor name.

diagrams.alt: Before: engineers sign in as IAM users with passwords and access keys. Seven AWS accounts sit in one organization. Bank supervisors would sign in to the dashboard with passwords kept in Callvale's Cognito user pool.
